mode.title: Mode
enumTitles: Posts by URL (metrics for known post/video URLs)
Diagnostic probe (fetch a few public URLs and report)
mode.description: A: look up known usernames. B: discover posts/creators by keyword. Posts: read metrics of known post/video URLs (TikTok). C: pull comments for known post URLs. To get comments alongside A, B or Posts in one run, use that mode and set fetchComments=true instead of running C separately. Expand: give known-good creators as usernames; the Actor reads their recent posts and comments, collects the accounts they mention and who interacts with them, then looks up and (optionally) screens those candidates.

platform.title: Platform
platform.description: Which social platform to scrape: TikTok, Instagram or Facebook.

usernames.title: Usernames (Mode A)
usernames.description: Handles/usernames to look up, without @ or full URL (e.g. "nasa").

postUrls.title: Post URLs (Mode C, or attached to A/B results)
postUrls.description: Direct post/video URLs to pull comments for. Only used directly in Mode C - in Mode A/B, use fetchComments instead.

maxResultsPerQuery.title: Max results per search query (Mode B default)
maxResultsPerQuery.description: Maximum number of results to return per search query (Mode B).

maxRecentPosts.title: Max recent posts per profile (Mode A)
maxRecentPosts.description: Maximum number of recent posts to fetch per profile (Mode A).

fetchComments.title: Also fetch comments (combined mode)
fetchComments.description: When true in Mode A or B, comment rows are fetched for every post returned and joined into the same dataset - no second run needed.

maxCommentsPerPost.title: Max comments per post
maxCommentsPerPost.description: Maximum number of comments to fetch per post (Mode C).

topLevelCommentsOnly.title: Top-level comments only (exclude replies)
topLevelCommentsOnly.description: If enabled, only fetch top-level comments and skip replies.

maxCandidates.title: Max candidates to look up (expand mode)
maxCandidates.description: Expand mode looks up the most frequently seen accounts, up to this many. Each lookup costs proxy traffic.

excludeUsernames.title: Already-known usernames to skip (expand mode)
excludeUsernames.description: Accounts you have already screened. They are never returned as candidates.

minFollowers.title: Screening: minimum followers
minFollowers.description: Optional. Rows get passesFilters/filterFailures set against the screening criteria you give. The Actor still returns the raw data.

requireContactEmail.title: Screening: require a contact email in the bio
requireContactEmail.description: Optional screening. When on, profiles without an e-mail address written in the bio get passesFilters=false with the reason. The Actor still returns the raw data.

excludeBioPatterns.title: Screening: fail if bio or link contains
excludeBioPatterns.description: For example stan.store, ebook, e-book. Case-insensitive text match on the bio and link URLs.

onlyPassing.title: Only write profiles that pass the screening
onlyPassing.description: Profiles that were read fine but fail the criteria are left out. Blocked or failed lookups are still written, never dropped silently.

followLinkInBio.title: Screening: follow link-in-bio pages
followLinkInBio.description: When you give 'fail if bio or link contains' patterns, profiles that pass the first checks have their link-in-bio pages (linktr.ee, beacons.ai, bio.link, carrd.co, stan.store and similar) opened and the destination links checked against the same patterns, so a shop hidden one click behind a Linktree is seen. A page that cannot be read is reported in screeningWarnings, never counted as clean.

reachPosts.title: Reach rule: number of latest posts to sample
reachPosts.description: 0 = off. When 4-6, profiles that pass the first screen get the median likes (and views, where shown) of their latest posts, as a percentage of followers: likesPctOfFollowers, viewsPctOfFollowers, reachPctOfFollowers. Costs one extra profile load plus one page per post, only for profiles that passed.

minReachPercent.title: Screening: minimum reach (% of followers)
minReachPercent.description: Optional, needs 'Reach rule' above. Profiles whose reachPctOfFollowers is below this (or cannot be computed) get passesFilters=false with the reason.

enrichSearchAuthors.title: Load each creator's profile page in search (Mode B)
enrichSearchAuthors.description: When true, every creator found by a keyword search also gets a full profile row (bio, links, contact email, exact follower count) by opening their profile page. Costs one extra page load per creator. When false, the profile row only carries what the search result itself showed.

maxItemsPerRun.title: Hard cap: max dataset items this run may write
maxItemsPerRun.description: Internal safety net in addition to the Actor run own maxItems/maxTotalChargeUsd call options.

sessionCookies.title: Login session cookie header (this platform only)
sessionCookies.description: Session cookie header for the selected platform, exported from a real logged-in browser session. Never a password.

proxyConfiguration.title: Proxy configuration
proxyConfiguration.description: Proxy configuration to use for requests. RESIDENTIAL is the default because these platforms block datacenter addresses much more often.

debugProbes.title: Diagnostic probes (mode = probe only)
debugProbes.description: Up to 12 items like {"url": "https://www.tiktok.com/@nasa", "type": "page"} or {"url": "...", "type": "fetch", "headers": {"x-ig-app-id": "..."}}. Optional per item: "grep": ["text", ...] (snippets around matches), "outline": {"selector": "[role=main]", "maxDepth": 10, "maxLines": 150} (compact DOM outline), "captureUrls": ["/api/post/item_list"] (records the JSON the page itself loads from matching URLs; with "scroll": 3 to scroll first and "click": "selector" to click once; "captureHead": 6000 for longer samples), "jsonScriptId" + "jsonPath": ["key", ...] (extract from an embedded JSON script). HTTPS GET on instagram/facebook/tiktok hosts only. Results are saved to the PROBE_RESULTS record. Reports what comes back, including login walls; it does not try to get past them.

maxProxyMegabytes.title: Hard cap: proxy traffic (MB) this run may use
maxProxyMegabytes.description: The run stops cleanly once the browser has moved this many megabytes (residential proxy is billed per GB). Set to 0 for no cap.

proxyPricePerGbUsd.title: Proxy price per GB (USD), for the cost report
proxyPricePerGbUsd.description: Optional. If set, the cost report also shows estimatedProxyUsd = megabytes/1000 x this price. Leave empty to see megabytes only.

blockHeavyResources.title: Block images, video and fonts
blockHeavyResources.description: Saves proxy traffic by not loading images, video and fonts. Off by default: TikTok returned an empty page when these were blocked. Try it on Instagram/Facebook to cut cost.

blockResourceTypes.title: Resource types to skip
blockResourceTypes.description: Types of files the browser is not allowed to download, to save proxy traffic. Default: media (video and audio streams; the TikTok creator page autoplays previews that otherwise cost a lot of proxy traffic). Blocking image and font together with media made TikTok return an empty page once, so add them only after testing.

standardUserAgent.title: Announce plain Chrome instead of HeadlessChrome
standardUserAgent.description: Headless Chromium puts 'HeadlessChrome' in its user agent, which some sites treat as a bot. This announces the same browser version as ordinary Chrome. It changes nothing else and does not hide automation.

fullChromium.title: Use full Chrome (new headless mode)
fullChromium.description: Runs Chrome's full 'new headless' mode instead of the stripped-down headless shell. Experiment for TikTok, which flags the default headless shell as a bot.

hideAutomationFlag.title: Do not set the automation flag
hideAutomationFlag.description: Leaves out Chromium's 'controlled by automation' flag (navigator.webdriver). Experiment for TikTok. Changes nothing else.

maxConcurrentRuns.title: Max runs of this Actor working at once
maxConcurrentRuns.description: A new run waits until fewer than this many OTHER runs that started earlier are still active (parallel browser runs made page loads time out). 0 = no limit.

concurrencyWaitMinutes.title: How long a run may wait for a free slot (minutes)
concurrencyWaitMinutes.description: After this the run ends without doing any work (OUTPUT.skipped = true) so the caller can retry later.
